title: A practical guide separates agent memory into compaction, retrieval and learned experience
friendlyTitle: Agent memory is really about rebuilding the right context
summary: A detailed engineering guide explains that an agent does not remember between model calls; its surrounding system must rebuild the right context. It compares lossy conversation compaction, retrieval from external stores and converting successful work into reusable procedures, using customer support as a running example.
friendlySummary: AI models do not remember earlier calls by themselves. The guide compares three ways to help: shorten recent history, retrieve old records and save useful lessons as reusable procedures.
whyItMatters: Reliable memory is an information-design problem, not merely a larger context window. Teams can improve agents by preserving provenance, retrieving only relevant records and promoting verified solutions into reusable knowledge rather than keeping every raw interaction.
friendlyWhyItMatters: A bigger context window does not automatically create good memory. Keep sources, retrieve only what matters and save proven solutions in a clear form.
